relationships.subject: CNR2
relationships.evidence_quote: Strikingly, CD3 + T cell populations were nearly absent in the PF of CNR2 k/o mice with EM, regardless of lesion types (UnD and DD), when compared to other groups (Figure 4C and F).

relationships.subject: CNR2
relationships.evidence_quote: Combined, our findings show that CNR2 is critical in T cell survival upon TCR activation with pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs)/danger-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) or antigen-mediated signals.

key_findings: CNR2 knockout mice with endometriosis lack peritoneal CD3+ T cells; CNR2-deficient T cells show reduced viability on activation.
CNR1 and CNR2 loss altered lesion transcriptome, immune pathways and microenvironment.
